title: C-Style Strings and Null Terminators
learningObjectives: Explain C-style string storage and null termination.
Recognize the terminator and buffer capacity.
Use string length functions with required headers.
Prevent buffer overrun and missing terminator errors.
Prefer std::string for safer text handling when appropriate.

understand.concept: C-style strings are character arrays ending with '\0'. C-string routines rely on a valid terminator.
understand.whyItMatters: Low-level interfaces and legacy code use null-terminated text.
understand.explain: Allocate room for the terminator and prevent buffer overflows.

examples.title: Null-terminated buffer
examples.explanation: The null character marks the end of a C string.

examples.title: Literal array
examples.code: char word[]="cat";\n// c, a, t and '\\0'

examples.title: C-string length
examples.code: char word[]="dog";\nstd::size_t n=std::strlen(word); // 3; include <cstring> for std::strlen
examples.explanation: strlen excludes the null terminator; include cstring.

examples.title: Buffer capacity
examples.code: char buffer[5]{};\n// up to 4 text characters plus '\\0'
examples.explanation: Capacity must include the terminator slot.

examples.title: Explicit termination
examples.explanation: The explicit terminator makes a valid C string.

practise.guidedTask: For C-Style Strings and Null Terminators, trace each example and record the collection type, size/capacity where relevant, valid index range, values before and after each operation, and what the code prints. Identify the key boundary case.
practise.independentTask: Write a C++ mini-task focused on C-Style Strings and Null Terminators: use a small collection of values/text, perform at least three meaningful operations, and test normal, empty or boundary, and invalid-index/input cases. Explain your collection choice and expected output.
hints: Select the collection type and justify its size behavior.
Trace initialization and current element values.
Use bounds-aware access for potentially invalid indexes.
Prefer direct traversal when the index is not required.
Test empty, first, last and out-of-range scenarios.
